title: Attention kernel thermostat: adaptive ramping & rollback thresholds for FlashAttention v2/v3
creator: Emily Chen
description: Problem: During mixed v2/v3 FlashAttention rollouts we've observed oscillatory latency and tail regressions for long-context decoder requests under bursty traffic. Root causes likely include abrupt kernel handoffs, non-gradual workspace allocation, and insufficient prefill pacing. Goal: Implement an adaptive 'thermostat' controller that smooths kernel ramping, exposes rollout-safe thresholds for rollback, and provides high-resolution telemetry for post-rollout analysis. This ticket scopes design, implementation, telemetry, canary policy, and rollback criteria for the thermostat controller.
acceptance_criteria: Controller available as an opt-in runtime policy flag (runtime.policy.attn_thermostat = on/off)
Measured 95th percentile decode latency reduced by >=10% vs current abrupt-handoff baseline on our long-context synthetic workload (seq_len >= 4096)
No more than 1.5x increase in average GPU memory workspace footprint during steady state compared to baseline allocations
Automatic soft-rollback triggers defined and tested in canary harness (latency/regression thresholds) and integrated with rollout pipeline
Telemetry dashboards showing thermostat state transitions, kernel choice probabilities, and workspace pressure for correlation
plan: Design phase: define thermostat state machine, inputs (latency, workspace pressure, kernel success/error rates), smoothing windows, and backoff rules
Prototype phase: implement in local runtime branch with configurable knobs for ramp rate, hysteresis, and emergency cutoff
Synthetic experiments: run against long-context and mixed-short workloads to tune parameters and measure memory/latency tradeoffs
Canary rollout: staged deployment to 1% of traffic with enhanced telemetry and automated rollback triggers
Iterate: adjust knobs, extend to Dedicated pools, document operational runbook, and add CI regression tests
tasks: Spec thermostat state machine and expose config (Emily)
Implement controller hooks in kernel selector and prefill pipeline (Rajiv)
Add telemetry spans and metrics: thermostat.phase, kernel_choice, workspace_bytes, kernel_fail_count (Telemetry team)
Create synthetic load harness for long-context decode scenarios (Benchmarking)
Author canary playbook and automated rollback script (SRE)
Run two tuning experiments and record parameter choices + results in shared doc (Emily/Rajiv)
risks: Over-aggressive ramping could increase workspace fragmentation and OOM risk
Telemetry cardinality increase if we emit per-request thermostat state naively
Interaction with existing autoscaling and batching heuristics may create emergent scheduling behaviors
Rollback thresholds too loose could delay mitigation for real regressions
